body.statement: From \(Q=n^2 2^{n-1}\) nontrivial oracle answers, \(\operatorname{Alg}_E\) returns \((G^\star,\operatorname{Comp}(G))\) over the full candidate universe \(U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow}\); for every directed edge, bidirected edge, directed loop, or bidirected loop \(e\in E(G^\star)\), \(e\in\operatorname{Comp}(G)\) iff \(\Sigma_E(G^\star-e)\neq\Sigma_E(G^\star)\).
body.justification: It converts existence into exact structure identification.
body.gap: Greatest-plus-compelled recovery exists for \(\mu\), not mixed E-separation.
body.consumer: Discovery reports compelled, optional, and impossible process mechanisms.

obligation.what_is_open: Show that the componentwise union enumerated from the singleton oracle is itself E-equivalent to the unknown graph over the unrestricted finite-DMG class.
obligation.obstruction: The finite query reduction and enumeration compute the union exactly, but identifying that observable union with an in-class greatest representative is precisely unrestricted union closure.
obligation.attempted: The singleton table was reduced to \(Q=n^2 2^{n-1}\) nontrivial queries, exhaustive graph enumeration was specified, and the compelled-edge deletion equivalence was proved conditional on greatestness.  No independent route makes the enumerated unrestricted union E-equivalent without resolving transfer or union closure.
obligation.partial_result:
The queried table has
\[
 n^2\,\bigl|\{C:C\subseteq V\setminus\{a\}\}\bigr|
 =n^2 2^{n-1}=Q
\]
entries.  Every omitted singleton query has \(a\in C\), so its source \(a_0\) belongs to \(D(\{b\},C)\) and the query is separated.  Thus the queried table determines the full singleton signature, and singleton composition determines \(\mathcal I_E\).  Since \(\mathfrak D(V)\) is finite, exhaustive comparison with this table computes both the componentwise union and the edge intersection of all matching graphs.  Conditional on unrestricted union closure, the computed union is the in-class graph \(G^\star\).

For the compelled-edge test, fix \(e\in E(G^\star)\).  If \(\Sigma_E(G^\star-e)=\Sigma_E(G^\star)\), composition makes \(G^\star-e\) E-equivalent to \(G^\star\), so an equivalent graph omits \(e\) and \(e\notin\operatorname{Comp}(G)\).  Conversely, if \(e\notin\operatorname{Comp}(G)\), some \(K\equiv_EG\) omits \(e\).  Greatestness yields
\[
 K\subseteq G^\star-e\subseteq G^\star,
\]
and the interval property yields \(G^\star-e\equiv_EG^\star\), hence equal signatures.  Taking contrapositives proves
\[
 e\in\operatorname{Comp}(G)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Sigma_E(G^\star-e)\ne\Sigma_E(G^\star).
\]
The enumeration, query count, and deletion criterion are therefore complete; only the unrestricted in-class union assertion remains open.
